deep.reconstruction:
Context. The upper two thirds of the page are drafts of two business letters about the estate of Riemann's late brother (died 1857): repayment of a loan of 1000 Th. Courant received through the banker Breusing in Osnabrück, and receipt of a 4% Hanoverian bond Lit. B No. 314 for 2000 Th. plus 43 Th. 27 Gr. in Prussian notes, settling an inheritance at Haselünne. The bottom third is scratch work for Riemann's 1860 memoir 'Über die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite'. The notation is the memoir's own:
- p = φ(ρ) is the pressure as a function of density.
- c = sqrt(φ'(ρ)) is the sound speed.
- f(ρ) = ∫ sqrt(φ'(ρ)) dρ/ρ.
- The Riemann invariants are defined by f(ρ)+u = 2r and f(ρ)−u = 2s, both written on the page.
- r is constant along dx/dt = u+c and s along dx/dt = u−c.

(1) Splitting of an initial disturbance. The initial state is constant outside a finite interval:
- x<a: r = R1, s = S1;
- x>b: r = R2, s = S2;
- a<x<b: arbitrary (the empty bracketed column).
The page then gives the state in the region that opens up between the two outgoing waves: r = R1, s = S2. My justification: forward characteristics entering it come from x<a, backward ones from x>b. Hence:
- u = r − s, and from f(ρ) − u = 2S2 one gets u = f(ρ) − 2S2, as written.
- In the forward simple wave s ≡ S2. A given density there travels with speed c+u = sqrt(φ'(ρ)) + f(ρ) − 2S2, which is a function of ρ alone.
- d/dρ of this speed equals c'(ρ) + c/ρ, which is positive for ordinary gases. So larger densities propagate faster.
The verbal remark (partly struck) says this: the larger values (of density) travel faster. In a compression wave the leading part therefore steepens (it 'becomes ever shorter', struck). The rarefaction wave ('Verdünnungswelle') widens and slows. This is the steepening argument of §§3–4 of the memoir.

(2) Separation time. The quantities sqrt(φ'(ρ1)) + u1 and sqrt(φ'(ρ2)) − u2 are the outward characteristic speeds at the two ends of the disturbed interval. Their sum divided by (b−a) is the inverse of a rough time (b−a)/(c1+u1+c2−u2) after which the two waves separate. This is a heuristic estimate; the interpretation of the fraction is mine.

(3) Polytropic case. For φ(ρ) = Aρ^k:
- c = sqrt(Ak)·ρ^((k−1)/2) and f = 2c/(k−1), so c = (k−1)/2·(r+s).
- Hence sqrt(φ'(ρ)) + u = (k+1)/2·r + (k−3)/2·s, as on the page.
- By symmetry, c − u = (k−3)/2·r + (k+1)/2·s.
The line 'r durchschnittlich um (1+k)/(3−k)·(r'−r'')' states an average change of r proportional to (1+k)/(3−k) times a jump r'−r''. It is probably connected with the shock (Verdichtungsstoß) relations or with comparing the speed coefficients (k+1)/2 and (3−k)/2. Its derivation is not on the page, so its exact meaning is unsure.

(4) Hodograph form and onset of the shock. Following the memoir, take x, t as functions of (r,s) with a potential w:
- x − (u+c)t = ∂w/∂r;
- x − (u−c)t = −∂w/∂s.
In the forward simple wave s is constant. Differentiate the first relation in x at fixed t (my step):
- 1 − t·∂(u+c)/∂r·∂r/∂x = ∂²w/∂r²·∂r/∂x.
- Next, ∂u/∂r = 1 and ∂ρ/∂r = ρ/c (since f'(ρ) = c/ρ).
- So ∂c/∂r = d log c / d log ρ, giving ∂(u+c)/∂r = d log sqrt(φ') / d log ρ + 1.
This yields exactly the page's ∂r/∂x·[∂²w/∂r² + t(∂log sqrt(φ'ρ)/∂log ρ + 1)] = 1. The analogous formula with ∂²w/∂s² covers the backward wave. The gradient ∂r/∂x becomes infinite, and a compression shock forms, at the first t where the bracket vanishes. This is the blow-up criterion used in the memoir.
errors: Second hodograph formula: with Riemann's convention x−(u−c)t = −∂w/∂s and r fixed, the correct relation is ∂s/∂x·[∂²w/∂s² + t(1 + d log c/d log ρ)] = −1. The page (as transcribed) has ∂r/∂x and right-hand side +1, so either a slip or a different sign convention for w in the draft. The prefactor ∂r/∂x should in any case be ∂s/∂x.

The expression (sqrt(φ'(ρ1))+sqrt(φ'(ρ2))+u1−u2)/(b−a) is a rate (inverse time), not a time. As a separation-time estimate it is only heuristic, because the characteristic speeds inside (a,b) differ from the boundary values.
The meaning and derivation of '(1+k)/(3−k)(r'−r'')' is not recoverable from the page; it cannot be verified.

deep.surprise_reason: These are preparatory notes for Riemann's published 1860 Luftwellen memoir, using its exact notation and results (Riemann invariants, wave splitting, polytropic speeds, shock-formation criterion). They add only biographical colour (estate letters c. 1857–59 on the same sheet).

transcription_corrections: 'Hasselüne' should be 'Haselünne' (town in the Emsland near Osnabrück).
In the scratch table the struck column head is 'x>b'; the middle-region entries read 'r=R1, s=S2' (the state between the separated waves).

The verbal note likely reads 'größere Werthe von ρ pflanzen sich mit größerer Geschwindigkeit fort' ('Dichte' possibly replacing a struck word), and 'die Verdünnungswelle ... verlangsamt/verbreitet sich'.
In the second hodograph formula the prefactor is probably ∂s/∂x rather than ∂r/∂x (check image).
'Hann. Landes[?]. Obligation' is uncertain; the reading of the bond type should be checked against the image.
